## What landed

**New crate `hh-xcheck` — the `hh-xcheck-bundle/1` replay package.**
`export_bundle` writes the committed golden corpora as a
language-neutral, self-describing bundle under
`crates/hh-xcheck/fixtures/cross-impl/` (94 members, committed —
generated deterministically, `export` → byte-identical):

| arm | input | answer | DF row |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity-trees` | 21 tree manifests + canonical renderings | `tree/1` ids | DF-S1.2-2 |
| `identity-records` | blob/text bytes + record canonical preimages | `version_id`/`semantic_id` | DF-S1.2-2 |
| `ledger-transcript` | the pinned `events.wal` verbatim + envelopes + scenario | `event_hashes`, `head_hash` | DF-S1.5-3 |
| `registry-snapshot` | canonical `registry.json` + scenario | `expected-outputs.json` bytes + digest | DF-S1.8-1 |
| `plugin-manifests` | the committed valid/invalid fixtures | `admit:<id>`/`refuse:<kind>` verdicts | DF-S1.27-1 |
| `canonical-parse` | 4×16 KiB + 2×64 KiB self-canonical frames | `sha256` digests | DF-S0.3-2 |

`CHECKER.md` travels inside the bundle — canonical-JSON rule, `idp/1`,
`tree/1`, the WAL `prev_hash` fold, the plugin verdict spellings, the
`answers.json` contract. `bundle.json` carries the per-member sha256
inventory, the arm→DF-row table, and `pending_cells[]` — the foreign
cells, each `environment-pending` on `HUMAN-H3`.

**`self_check` — the hermetic E1 replay.** Replays every arm through
the E1 primitives from the serialized inputs alone (manifest →
canonical → id; WAL → chain head; log → snapshot outputs; manifest
bytes → verdicts): **55/55 cases green**. Export refuses to proceed if
the ledger transcript drifts from the pinned golden head.

**`verify_answers` — the foreign-side comparator.** Diffs a foreign
`answers.json` against `expected` case-by-case: missing or disagreeing
cases fail by name — never a vacuous pass. Timing members are carried,
not gated. (Smoke: exact answers 49/0 green; a doctored digest and a
dropped case both fail named.)

**`hh-identity` additive accessors.** `Tree::entries`/`canonical_json`
and `corpus::golden_tree_fixtures`/`golden_record_fixtures` expose the
corpus inputs for serialization; `golden_trees()`/`golden_records()`
derive from them unchanged — every pinned golden id, the five-record
corpus, and ordering preserved (golden_corpus battery green).
